subject: Incorrect Model DF for Partial Credit Model

messages.author: 0734be0d439c3900
messages.subject: Incorrect Model DF for Partial Credit Model
parts:
Hi - 

I want to estimate a partial credit model with an estimated common slope instead of using the Rasch option which forces all slopes = 1. My data consists of three items with three response options (1, 2, and 3). I attempted to constrain the slopes to equality using the following commands. 

First, obtain parameter names/numbers for the model

library(mirt)
values.gpcm <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", verbose=FALSE, pars='values')
print(values.gpcm)

That produced the following.



Next I specified that slopes 1 8 and 15 are constrained.

library(mirt)
results.pcm <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", verbose=FALSE, simplify=F, constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15)))
coef.pcmirt <- coef(results.pcm, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE)
coef.pcmglfa <- coef(results.pcm, IRTpars=FALSE, simplify=TRUE)
print(results.pcm)
print(coef.pcmirt)
print(coef.pcmglfa)

The results match estimates from Stata except the model degrees of freedom are incorrect. Instead of 7 (6 thresholds and 1 slope), mirt reports 9 (6 thresholds and 3 slopes) despite the three slopes constrained to equality. 

I tried setting the estimation of slopes 8 and 15 to false, 

values.gpcm [1, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [1, "est"] = TRUE
values.gpcm [8, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [8, "est"] = FALSE
values.gpcm [15, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [15, "est"] = FALSE

and running this code instead

results.pcm1 <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", pars = values.gpcm,  verbose=FALSE, simplify=F, constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15)) )
coef.pcmirt1 <- coef(results.pcm1, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE)
coef.pcmglfa1 <- coef(results.pcm1, IRTpars=FALSE, simplify=TRUE)
print(results.pcm1)
print(coef.pcmirt1)
print(coef.pcmglfa1)

and that worked to provide the correct model df, but I got this error message when trying to requet IRT parameters. 

> coef.pcmirt1 <- coef(results.pcm1, IRTpars=TRUE, simplify=TRUE) Error in ret[obj@est, obj@est] <- vcov[pick, pick, drop = FALSE] : number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

If I omit that line and omit print the IRT line, the code runs fine and produces the results expected. I can manually convert the slope-intercept to IRT, but I would like for mirt to produce those instead with the correct df. 

Any ideas how to obtain PCM estimates, non-Rasch, with correct model df?

Thanks!
Bryan

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Incorrect Model DF for Partial Credit Model
parts:
Hi Bryan,

This looks like it was a printing mistake as the degrees of freedom are correctly tracked elsewhere (e.g., anova(mod0, mod1) gives the correct difference). I've pushed the fix to the dev version (1.44.1), so if you want the fix feel free to install.

Regarding the second issue, that's less clear to me, though try updating and see if the issue remains. Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 0734be0d439c3900
messages.subject: Re: Incorrect Model DF for Partial Credit Model
parts:
Hi Phil - 

Thanks for the reply and update. Version 1.44.1 reported the correct model df now for the first set of commands in which slopes 1 8 and 15 were estimated but constrained (i.e., constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15))). 

The second set of commands using the pars command (i.e., pars = values.gpcm) also ran without issue but reported 5 instead of 7 model df. Below is a list of parameters post-estimation showing 7 estimated despite 5 df reported. Recall I used potentially odd constraints: estimate 1, not 8 and 15, then constrain 8 and 15 = estimate for 1 so maybe that is the problem.

values.gpcm [1, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [1, "est"] = TRUE
values.gpcm [8, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [8, "est"] = FALSE
values.gpcm [15, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [15, "est"] = FALSE
results.pcm1 <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", pars = values.gpcm,  verbose=FALSE, simplify=F, constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15)) )

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Incorrect Model DF for Partial Credit Model
parts:
This looks correct to me as you're trying to apply an equality constraint to a parameter that is fixed at a constant, so it doesn't really do anything (if you want to use equality constraints the parameter $est must be TRUE). It's interesting that this doesn't throw an error as if this were defined using the syntax an error would be raised. It's possible the sanity check is just too early when the data.frame of parameters is supplied; thanks for putting this on my radar.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Incorrect Model DF for Partial Credit Model
parts: Sanity check for this setup now runs a little later in the chain, so is properly caught and returns an error. The fix would be:

values.gpcm [1, "value"] = 1
values.gpcm [1, "est"] = TRUE
values.gpcm [8, "value"] = 1
#values.gpcm [8, "est"] = FALSE
values.gpcm [15, "value"] = 1
#values.gpcm [15, "est"] = FALSE
results.pcm1 <- mirt(data=toxic202122c3, model=1, itemtype="gpcm", SE=TRUE, method = "QMCEM", pars = values.gpcm,  verbose=FALSE, simplify=F, constrain=list(c(1, 8, 15)) )

to match the estimation logic as equality constrained parameters are not fixed during estimation. Thanks for the report.

Phil
